EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
Nida Experiment Card PC130 - 14A
In this lesson, you will troubleshoot a faulted RC transient circuit.
INTRODUCTIONM
The input signal is altered depending upon its frequency and the RC time constant of the circuit..
Measuring the waveforms with an oscilloscope determines if the circuit is operating normally.
An incorrect waveform indicates that the circuit is faulted.
Let's begin the lesson on RC CIRCUIT TRANSIENT TROUBLESHOOTING EXPERIMENT.
LESSON MENU
RC CIRCUIT TRANSIENT FAULTS
The most common fault in RC transient circuits is an open or shorted component.
DISCUSSION
Changed value components do occur, but are less frequent than opens and shorts.
For the circuit to operate correctly, all components must function correctly.
In this RC circuit, the frequency allows the capacitor to fully charge and discharge in 5 time constants. The output waveform is taken across the resistor. 7
If C1 opens internally, the input is dropped across it and no current flows through the capacitor.
The voltage across R1 drops to zero because current cannot flow through the open series capacitor.
The entire input signal is present across the capacitor and is unaltered.
A circuit with an extremely short time constant or extremely low frequency has similar characteristics because of high capacitive reactance.
A circuit with an extremely short time constant or extremely low frequency has similar characteristics because of high capacitive reactance.

CAPACITIVE REACTANCE - Although capacitive reactance is calculated differently for square wave and sine wave circuits, the same principles apply.
If C1 shorts internally, the circuit has no effect on the input signal other than the load of R1. The input signal is measured across R1.
Current bypasses the capacitor. C1 is effectively not in the circuit and no waveform is present across the capacitor.
If R1 opens internally, the waveform across it is identical to the input signal except it is AC.
The capacitor blocks the DC component and passes only the AC.
The capacitor blocks the DC component and passes only the AC.
DC COMPONENT - The waveform shown is a DC square wave from 0V to 2V. The DC component is the average DC level or 1V.
DEFINITION
It should be noted that if R1 and C1 are in opposite positions C1 cannot block the DC component.
A circuit with an extremely long time constant or extremely high frequency has similar characteristics.
A circuit with an extremely long time constant or extremely high frequency has similar characteristics.
CAPACITIVE REACTANCE - When capacitive reactance decreases less signal is dropped across the capacitor and more signal is dropped across the resistor.
CAPACITIVE REACTANCE - Although capacitive reactance is calculated differently for square wave circuits and sine wave circuits, the same principles apply.
If the resistor shorts, there is no signal across it.
The entire input signal is dropped across C1 and is unaltered.
These are the same indications as for an open capacitor. Measuring the resistance of R1 determines if R1 is shorted or if C1 is open.

TRY AGAIN!
If R1 is shorted, the signal is grounded and there is no waveform. Notice the waveform across R1..
TRY AGAIN!
A changed value component changes the RC time constant of the circuit.
An increase in resistance or capacitance increases the time constant.
A decrease in resistance or capacitance decreases the time constant.
A resistance measurement is necessary to determine if the capacitor or the resistor changed value.
If the resistor checks good, then the capacitor is the changed value component.
If the resistor does not check good, then it is the changed value component. This method of locating the component eliminates the need for an RCL bridge.
If the resistor does not check good, then it is the changed value component. This method of locating the component eliminates the need for an RCL bridge.
RCL BRIDGE - An RCL bridge is a piece of electronic test equipment that determines the resistance of resistors, capacitance of capacitors, and inductance of inductors.
This chart will help you remember what to look for when troubleshooting.
FAULT CAPACITOR WAVEFORM RESISTOR WAVEFORM
Open Capacitor Identical to input Zero waveform
Shorted Capacitor Zero waveform Identical to input
Open Resistor DC component of input AC portion of the input
Shorted Resistor Identical to input Zero waveform
Changed Value Component Indicates erroneous RC Indicates erroneous RC
What type of faults produce no waveform across the resistor?
An open R1 or shorted C1 would not cause the waveform across R1 to be zero.
TRY AGAIN!
A changed value R1 and C1 would not cause the waveform across R1 to be zero.
TRY AGAIN!
